title: (Approximately) 10 Things That Vanished Mysteriously
summary: Josh and Chuck cover roughly ten famous unexplained disappearances. They open with small talk about cooking smells and David Copperfield's Statue of Liberty illusion, then discuss Solomon Northup's disappearance after his book tour, Jimmy Hoffa's 1975 vanishing outside Detroit and the theories about his body, and the Alcatraz escape of Frank Morris and the Anglin brothers. Next is Helen Brock, the candy heiress who vanished after a Mayo Clinic visit, with suspect Richard Bailey. They then cover George Washington's stolen dentures from the Smithsonian, Flight 19 and the Bermuda Triangle, the Mary Celeste ghost ship, and John Brisker, the basketball player who vanished in Uganda. The episode ends with listener mail and a sign-off.

segments.title: Opening banter and Copperfield's Statue of Liberty
segments.summary: Josh and Chuck open with small talk about cooking smells and stove hoods, then transition to David Copperfield making the Statue of Liberty disappear and the idea of famous disappearances.

segments.title: Solomon Northup's disappearance
segments.summary: The hosts describe Solomon Northup, the free-born man kidnapped into slavery and author of Twelve Years a Slave. After his book tour he vanished; the last record is from 1863. Theories include being a Union spy, being recaptured, assuming a new identity, or dying unidentified.

segments.title: Jimmy Hoffa
segments.summary: Jimmy Hoffa's feud with Bobby Kennedy, his pardon by Nixon, and his disappearance on July 30, 1975 outside Detroit. Theories about his body include burial at Giants Stadium, a shallow grave near the restaurant, alligators, and a wood chipper. A 2014 book claimed half his body was buried in a barn, but the FBI found nothing.

segments.title: Alcatraz escape of 1962
segments.summary: Frank Morris and the Anglin brothers escaped Alcatraz in 1962 using a carved vent, paper-mache heads, and raincoat life vests. Alan West was left behind. A body was seen floating, and a life vest with human teeth marks was found, but the men were never confirmed dead or alive.

segments.title: Helen Brock disappearance
segments.summary: Candy heiress Helen Brock vanished after a 1977 Mayo Clinic visit. Her house man Jack Matlick gave conflicting accounts, and checks bearing her forged signature were cashed. Richard Bailey, a swindler, was sentenced to thirty years and suspected of involvement. Her brother burned her diaries, saying she was into automatic writing.

segments.title: Break
segments.summary: Mid-episode break with banter about a TV true crime show and casting.

segments.title: George Washington's stolen dentures
segments.summary: George Washington's dentures, on loan from the University of Maryland dental school, were stolen from a Smithsonian storage room. Half reappeared about a year later, and the top set is still missing. The hosts discuss where the teeth came from, including questions about slave teeth.

segments.title: Flight 19 and the Bermuda Triangle
segments.summary: Five TBM Avenger torpedo bombers vanished in December 1945 on a training flight from Fort Lauderdale. The flight leader reported faulty compasses. A rescue Mariner also vanished. A later wreck found in the Everglades may be one of the planes, and the hosts note the Close Encounters connection.

segments.title: Mary Celeste ghost ship
segments.summary: The Mary Celeste was found abandoned in December 1872 about 400 miles east of the Azores, with no one aboard and a lifeboat missing. Theories include leaky barrels of industrial alcohol, a hasty abandonment, and a possible crew conspiracy. The salvage award was reduced to one sixth of the insured value.

segments.title: John Brisker's vanishing in Uganda
segments.summary: Former ABA and SuperSonics player John Brisker went to Uganda under Idi Amin's invitation and disappeared after calling his girlfriend. Theories include being killed by Amin's soldiers or by anti-Amin revolutionaries, and a far-fetched Jonestown link. His brother believed he had assumed a new identity.

segments.title: Listener mail
segments.summary: Thanks to listeners and companies for candy, books, sauces, CDs, and other gifts, and a shout-out to a restaurant manager.

segments.title: Sign-off
segments.summary: Hosts give contact information and sign off.
